newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SOCCER-RAIN FORCES POSTPONEMENT OF WORLD CUP CLASH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RAIN FORCES POSTPONEMENT OF WORLD CUP CLASH.

text.p: Australia soccer officials faced logistical problems and a financial loss after torrential rain forced the postponement of the Oceania group World Cup play-off second leg against New Zealand on Saturday.

Australia, who hold a 3-0 lead from the previous Saturday's first leg in Auckland, will now play New Zealand on Sunday at a different ground after the deluge left the Sydney Football Stadium waterlogged.
Soccer Australia chairman David Hill said the need to hire a second ground at short notice would greatly add to costs.
"Apart from the disappointment for players and supporters alike, financially it's going to be a problem. We've hired two grounds now," Hill said.
The ruling body could also lose at the gate after being forced to switch the game from a 42,000-capacity ground to the smaller 25,000-seater Parramatta Stadium in western Sydney.
The winner of the tie will play an Asian opponent later this year for a place in the 1998 World Cup finals in France.
